identification.summary: SneakyChef is the name Cisco Talos uses for a Chinese-speaking espionage actor that uses SugarGh0st, a customized variant of Gh0st RAT, and later also the SpiceRAT implant, against government foreign-affairs targets [S1][S2][S2]. Talos believes the SugarGh0st campaign likely began as early as August 2023 [S1].
identification.firstObserved: Talos: likely as early as August 2023 [S1].
identification.notes: Vendor boundary: Proofpoint tracks a May 2024 SugarGh0st campaign against US AI organizations as UNK_SweetSpecter and did not confidently link it to a known actor; this is not merged with SneakyChef here [S4][S5]. Talos's original SugarGh0st post (Nov 2023) assessed Chinese-speaking authorship with low confidence; its later SneakyChef reporting (2024) states medium confidence; a Talos conference abstract says high [S1][S2].

attribution.confidence: Talos assesses the operators are likely Chinese-speaking: low confidence in the Nov 2023 SugarGh0st post [S1], medium confidence in its 2024 SneakyChef reporting [S2]; a later Talos conference abstract says high. Talos has not tied the group to a specific government [S2].
attribution.basis: Language artifacts, Gh0st RAT lineage (source code publicly released in 2008 and popular with Chinese-speaking actors), and government targeting [S1][S2].

regions: Uzbekistan and South Korea (initial SugarGh0st campaign) [S1]
Latvia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, India, Angola and the Royal Embassy of Saudi Arabia (expanded targeting reported in 2024) [S2]
targeting.notes: Talos found evidence the early campaign targeted the Uzbekistan Ministry of Foreign Affairs and users in South Korea, with decoy documents in Uzbek and Korean [S1]. Later lures were scanned government documents tied to foreign ministries and embassies, including an Indian passport application form and a document impersonating the Embassy of Lithuania; SpiceRAT in Angola used lures from a Turkmenistan news agency [S2]. The US AI-organization campaign is Proofpoint's UNK_SweetSpecter, not attributed to SneakyChef [S4].

capabilities.summary: SugarGh0st is a customized Gh0st RAT with tailored remote-administration commands and an altered communication protocol; it supports remote control, keylogging, webcam access and downloading arbitrary binaries [S1]. Later variants add reconnaissance such as searching for specific keys and file extensions, collecting hostname, filesystem, drive and OS details, and desktop screenshots [S2]. Talos documented two infection chains in 2023: a RAR archive with an LNK that runs a JavaScript dropper, and a DynamicWrapperX loader that injects shellcode [S1]. In 2024 Talos reported delivery shifting to self-extracting RAR archives, and a second implant, SpiceRAT, delivered via LNK and HTA chains with DLL side-loading, sometimes from the same sender address as SugarGh0st emails [S2].

campaigns.name: SugarGh0st against Uzbekistan and South Korea
campaigns.summary: Talos believes the campaign likely began as early as August 2023, using Uzbek- and Korean-language decoys and two infection chains to deliver SugarGh0st; Talos reported it in November 2023.

campaigns.name: SugarGh0st against US AI organizations (UNK_SweetSpecter, Proofpoint)
campaigns.summary: Proofpoint reported AI-themed lures sent from a free email account to fewer than ten people tied to one US AI organization, with a chain resembling Talos's earlier description and a new C2 domain. Proofpoint did not confidently link it to a known actor, so it is a related but separate vendor cluster.

campaigns.name: Expanded foreign-ministry targeting and SpiceRAT
campaigns.summary: Talos reported SneakyChef widening to ministries of foreign affairs in Latvia, Kazakhstan, Turkmenistan, India and Angola plus the Royal Embassy of Saudi Arabia, introducing SpiceRAT, and shifting to self-extracting RAR delivery.

diamond.adversary: Chinese-speaking operators, medium-confidence assessment by Talos (2024); no government sponsor identified [S2].
diamond.capability: SugarGh0st (custom Gh0st RAT), SpiceRAT, LNK/HTA/RAR/self-extracting RAR delivery, DynamicWrapperX loader, DLL side-loading [S1][S2].
diamond.infrastructure: Old and new C2 domains are referenced in the existing record; the Proofpoint-tracked cluster used account.gommask[.]online on AS142032 (UNK_SweetSpecter, not attributed to SneakyChef) [S4]. Other infrastructure details were not retrieved.
diamond.victim: Foreign ministries and embassies in Central Asia, South Asia, Europe, Africa, the Middle East and South Korea [S1][S2].
diamond.socioPolitical: Targets suggest diplomatic and foreign-policy intelligence interest; no source states a specific tasking [S2].
diamond.technology: Windows endpoints reached through spear-phishing with archive, shortcut and HTA files [S1][S2].

gaps: Talos primary blog posts (new-sugargh0st-rat, new-spicerat-sneakychef, and the SneakyChef post) could not be fetched in this session (host unreachable); content is taken from search-result summaries and secondary coverage. Exact publication dates are approximate to month.
No sponsor, government attribution, or MITRE group ID identified; no Microsoft naming found.
Relationship between UNK_SweetSpecter (Proofpoint) and SneakyChef is not established in sources gathered.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Foreign-ministry and embassy mail systems and the personal accounts of diplomatic staff are key terrain. STEP 2: The actor is a low-cost phishing operator using a modified commodity RAT, with delivery formats changed between campaigns (RAR/LNK, HTA, self-extracting RAR) [S1][S2]. STEP 3: Template is spear-phish with a government-themed scanned decoy, then archive or shortcut execution, then SugarGh0st or SpiceRAT with reconnaissance and screenshot collection [S2]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued phishing of foreign ministries and embassies in Asia, Europe, Africa and the Middle East. MDCOA is retargeting of allied or partner diplomatic staff and defense-related organizations, as the Proofpoint-observed AI-sector use of the same malware family suggests [S4]. Candidate indicators: LNK or HTA attachments inside RAR or self-extracting archives, DLL side-loading from user-writable paths, and Gh0st-style custom C2 protocol traffic.
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: track Talos and Proofpoint reporting and share indicators with coalition partners whose foreign ministries are named targets [S2]. (2) Authorities: partner-network defense relies on host-nation or bilateral arrangements, not US authorities. (3) Mission assurance: block or sandbox archive, LNK and HTA attachments and brief personnel on government-themed lures. (4) Coordination: route indicators through the COPC and DC3 channels; do not treat the Proofpoint and Talos clusters as one actor without further evidence [S4].

provenance.importedSummary: SneakyChef is a threat actor known for using the SugarGh0st RAT to target government agencies, research institutions, and organizations worldwide. They have been active since at least August 2023, with a focus on leveraging old and new command and control domains. The group has been observed using lures in the form of scanned documents related to Ministries of Foreign Affairs and embassies. Talos Intelligence assesses with medium confidence that the operators are likely Chinese-speaking based on language preferences and specific targets.
